violated_contract: A payload whose key order carries meaning to its consumer must reach that consumer in its authored order. A JSON schema handed to a constrained decoder is such a payload: llama.cpp compiles json_schema to a grammar that emits properties in listed order, and Apple FoundationModels guided generation follows DynamicGenerationSchema property order, so property order is generation order. Parsing it into an unordered dictionary (JSONSerialization, [String: Any]) and re-serializing or iterating it -- including iterating keys.sorted() -- silently replaces the authored order with a hash or alphabetical one. The request still succeeds and still validates, so the defect is invisible except as worse or non-terminating model output.
canonical_prevention: Carry order-bearing JSON as bytes and splice it verbatim, or read key order with an order-preserving scan; never rebuild it from an unordered container. Prove it with a test that captures the real bytes handed to the consumer (the HTTP body, the generated schema nodes) and asserts the authored order, not a test that compares parsed dictionaries, which are equal under any order.
